expected.older-root-mismatch: compute_roots yields an older root != R_m: rejected by the comparison with the trusted older root
expected.newer-root-mismatch: older root == R_m but newer root != R_n: rejected only by the COSE signature over the detached payload

valid.description: Smallest possible proof. m=1 is a power of two so the anchor is the older root, which is the first leaf itself; one right sibling (the second leaf).
Older tree perfect, newer tree one leaf larger. Anchor = older root; the single right sibling is a bare leaf hanging off the root.
Both trees perfect. Anchor = older root; one right sibling covering [4,8).
Older tree perfect, newer not. One right sibling covering the truncated range [4,6).

Adjacent sizes, older not a power of two. Anchor is leaf 4. Exercises a pass-through level: [4,6) is the last node of level 1 and a left child, so it has no sibling and emits nothing; the L element R[0,4) is its parent's sibling. Same tag string (RL) as 06.
Anchor is a 2-leaf subtree [4,6) (lowest set bit of 6). Same tag string (RL) as 05 with different sizes: tags alone do not determine sizes.
Older tree one leaf short of perfect. Anchor is leaf 6; every level has a sibling (no pass-through): R h7, L R[4,6), L R[0,4).
Anchor is the 4-leaf subtree [8,12); its right sibling in the newer tree is the bare leaf 12 (a sibling much smaller than the node it joins).
Anchor is leaf 8. Levels 1 and 2 are both pass-throughs (last node, left child), so after R h9 the next element is directly L R[0,8).
doc/tiles-illustrated.rst example 1: perfect older tree across the width-8 tile boundary; anchor = R[0,64), one right sibling R[64,70).
doc/tiles-illustrated.rst example 2: anchor is leaf 22; tags RLLRLRR; same tag string for any n in 65..70 (the newer size is not recoverable from the proof).
Mixed case: R h37, R R[38,40), L R[32,36), R R[40,45) (a truncated right sibling), then a pass-through and L R[0,32).
Anchor is the 4-leaf subtree [96,100) inside a much larger newer tree; 8 elements mixing shared and newer-only siblings.
Older tree of 3 leaves inside a perfect 65536-leaf newer tree: anchor is leaf 2, then R h3, L R[0,2), and 14 right siblings doubling in size up to R[32768,65536).
Longest path in the set: anchor = leaf 0 (= older root), 17 right siblings, doubling then truncated at the top.
Adjacent sizes near the top of the set: anchor is leaf 69998, one right sibling (leaf 69999) then only shared left siblings up to the root.

Constructed, not from merklecpp: anchor R[4,8) with an extra shared left sibling R[0,4) instead of the canonical anchor R[0,8). Sound and accepted, but longer than canonical; a canonical proof never starts with a left sibling.

An extra right sibling appended: older root still matches, newer root changes.

Last element (R[64,68), a newer-only right sibling) dropped: this is the valid proof 23 -> 64, so the older root matches and the newer root is R_64, not R_68. Only the signature over the payload distinguishes it.

A newer-only right sibling replaced by zeros: the OLDER root still matches; only the newer root (the detached payload) changes, so this is caught by the signature check, not by the older-root comparison.
First element re-tagged as left: both roots change.
Element 2 (a shared left sibling) re-tagged as right: both recomputed roots change.
Elements listed root-to-anchor instead of anchor-to-root: both roots change.
Anchor replaced by zeros: both roots change.
A shared left sibling replaced by zeros: both roots change.
